A/E Tutorial

The ratio of the maximum current amplitude A to the energy E of a pulse separates single-site events (SSE) from multi-site events (MSE) in a germanium detector. Background events near the Q-value of the neutrinoless double-beta decay are mostly multi-site, while the decay itself is single-site. This tutorial derives an energy-independent A/E classifier from a calibration spectrum and measures the fraction of events that survive a cut on it.

The workflow follows the A/E calibration of the Juleana.jl production and uses a synthetic Th-228 calibration spectrum, so that the example runs without any detector data. Also have a look at the manual page A/E Pulse-Shape Discrimination.

The example loads the packages and sets the plotting backend first. Plots are produced by lplot from LegendMakie, with the LEGEND watermarks switched off.

using CairoMakie
using Distributions
using LegendMakie
using LegendSpecFits
using Measurements
using Measurements: value as mvalue
using Random
using StatsBase
using Unitful
using Unitful: keV

CairoMakie.activate!(type = "png")

Generating Synthetic Events

The synthetic data set contains Compton continuum events and the Th-228 lines at 583.2, 727.3, 860.6, 1592.5 (double escape peak, DEP), 1620.5, 2103.5 (single escape peak, SEP) and 2614.5 keV (full energy peak, FEP). The energy resolution is Gaussian with a standard deviation of 0.75 keV + 0.00022 E.

Every event has an A/E value. Single-site events follow a Gaussian with an energy-dependent mean $\mu(E) = \mu_A + \mu_B E$ and standard deviation $\sigma(E) = \sqrt{\sigma_A^2 + \sigma_B^2 / E^2}$. Multi-site events are shifted to lower A/E by an exponentially distributed amount, in units of $\sigma(E)$. The multi-site fraction is small in the DEP, whose events are mostly single-site, and large in the SEP. The raw A/E scale is arbitrary and is multiplied by a constant, which the first step of the analysis removes.

Random.seed!(2024)

lines = (
    # energy (keV), number of events, multi-site fraction
    (583.2, 60_000, 0.3), (727.3, 20_000, 0.3), (860.6, 8_000, 0.3),
    (1592.5, 25_000, 0.12), (1620.5, 6_000, 0.4), (2103.5, 30_000, 0.75),
    (2614.5, 120_000, 0.35),
)
n_continuum = 1_200_000
resolution(E) = 0.75 + 0.00022 * E

e_lines = reduce(vcat, [E .+ resolution(E) .* randn(n) for (E, n, _) in lines])
e_continuum = 200 .+ rand(truncated(Exponential(800), 0, 2400), n_continuum)
e_keV = vcat(e_lines, e_continuum)
mse_fraction = vcat(reduce(vcat, [fill(f, n) for (_, n, f) in lines]), fill(0.25, n_continuum))

The A/E parameters of the single-site population are the values that the analysis recovers in the following sections.

μA, μB, σA, σB = 1.0, -4.0e-6, 5.0e-3, 12.0
sse_mean(E) = μA + μB * E
sse_sigma(E) = sqrt(σA^2 + σB^2 / E^2)

σ_sse = sse_sigma.(e_keV)
aoe_scale = 55.0
aoe_raw = aoe_scale .* (sse_mean.(e_keV) .+ σ_sse .* randn(length(e_keV)) .-
    (rand(length(e_keV)) .< mse_fraction) .* σ_sse .* rand(Exponential(6), length(e_keV)))
e_cal = e_keV .* u"keV"

Normalizing the Raw A/E

The raw A/E has an arbitrary scale. The function cut_single_peak locates the single-site peak in the distribution of all events, and dividing by the position of its maximum sets the peak to about one. The division is stored as a string expression, which the later fits extend to the full correction function.

cuts_aoe = cut_single_peak(aoe_raw, 0.0, quantile(filter(isfinite, aoe_raw), 0.99); n_bins = -1)
aoe_expression = "aoe / $(cuts_aoe.max)"
aoe = aoe_raw ./ cuts_aoe.max

The two-dimensional histogram of A/E against energy shows the single-site band, whose position and width depend on the energy, and the multi-site events below it.

h_aoe_raw = fit(Histogram, (e_keV, aoe), (0:5.0:3000, 0.5:0.005:1.3))
lhist(h_aoe_raw, figsize = (670, 400), watermark = false, rasterize = true,
    title = "Normalized A/E", xlabel = "Energy (keV)", ylabel = "A/E (a.u.)")

Fitting Compton Bands

The energy dependence of the single-site band is measured in narrow energy slices of the Compton continuum, called Compton bands. The bands avoid the peaks, so that their events are mostly Compton scattered. The function generate_aoe_compton_bands cuts the A/E values of every band into a histogram and estimates the position and width of the single-site peak. The band-wise fit needs at least 20 bands.

compton_bands = [500, 540, 620, 660, 760, 800, 900, 940, 1000, 1040, 1100, 1140, 1200, 1240,
    1300, 1340, 1400, 1440, 1500, 1540, 1660, 1700, 1760, 1800, 1860, 1900, 1960, 2000,
    2060, 2140, 2200, 2240, 2300, 2340] .* u"keV"
compton_window = 20.0u"keV"

compton_band_peakhists = generate_aoe_compton_bands(aoe, e_cal, compton_bands, compton_window)

The histogram of the first band shows the single-site peak and the tail of multi-site events toward low A/E.

lhist(compton_band_peakhists.peakhists[1], watermark = false,
    title = "A/E Compton band at $(compton_bands[1])", xlabel = "A/E (a.u.)", ylabel = "Counts")

The function fit_aoe_compton fits every band with a Gaussian for the single-site peak and an exponentially modified Gaussian for the multi-site background. It returns the results and reports as dictionaries keyed by the band energy.

result_fit, report_fit = fit_aoe_compton(compton_band_peakhists.peakhists,
    compton_band_peakhists.peakstats, compton_bands; uncertainty = true)
result_fit[compton_bands[1]]
(μ = 1.00737 ± 0.00024, σ = 0.02408 ± 0.00018, n = 16440.0 ± 160.0, B = 5320.0 ± 100.0, δ = 0.1498 ± 0.0054, fwhm = 0.058796 ± 2.5e-6, fit_func = :aoe_one_bck, gof = (pvalue = 0.7243058240099582, chi2 = 606.4714176655399, dof = 628, covmat = [5.687146237042773e-8 -1.4379823464774903e-8 … 0.009310843011917782 -4.7428372897844265e-7; -1.4379823464774903e-8 3.3346009474492577e-8 … -0.0055861439149197875 3.0244445090606675e-7; … ; 0.009310843011917782 -0.0055861439149197875 … 10635.074998485761 -0.11781116162462435; -4.7428372897844265e-7 3.0244445090606675e-7 … -0.11781116162462435 2.9574199514355725e-5], mean_residuals = 0.0025772944206161677, median_residuals = 0.06238883221955304, std_residuals = 0.9888055446445135, residuals_norm = [-0.5236714605128012, 0.8234617706683297, 0.15997983726468198, 0.8329859207777073, -1.1581710843760928, -0.4851665816644787, 1.5096900556026536, -1.1307133795660853, 0.856867245796956, 0.20362534669799476  …  -0.39677644148047625, 0.8695713148876514, 0.32910574326781566, -0.23962498531986096, 1.2104621199664949, -0.6207032163978637, 0.06600435216700064, -1.0130318910120064, -0.7396354718790549, 1.0443860777384504], converged = true))

The report of a band contains the data and the best fit, which lplot draws with the fit residuals.

lplot(report_fit[compton_bands[1]], watermark = false)

Bands whose fit did not converge are removed before the energy dependence is fitted. The accepted bands provide the position μ and width σ of the single-site peak with uncertainties.

good_bands = findall(b -> haskey(result_fit, b) && result_fit[b].gof.converged, compton_bands)
compton_bands = compton_bands[good_bands]
μ = [result_fit[b].μ for b in compton_bands]
σ = [result_fit[b].σ for b in compton_bands]
length(good_bands)
34

Fitting the Energy Dependence

The function fit_aoe_corrections fits a straight line to the band positions and $\sqrt{\sigma_A^2 + \sigma_B^2 / E^2}$ to the band widths. The result also contains the string func, which expresses the normalized classifier $(A/E - \mu(E)) / \sigma(E)$ in terms of the variables aoe and e.

result_fit_single, report_fit_single = fit_aoe_corrections(compton_bands, μ, σ;
    aoe_expression = aoe_expression, e_expression = "e")
result_fit_single.µ_compton.par
2-element Vector{Number}:
   1.00933 ± 0.0001
 -3.959e-6 ± 6.7e-8 keV^-1

The fitted position of the single-site peak decreases linearly with the energy.

lplot(report_fit_single.report_μ, watermark = false)

The fitted width decreases with the energy.

lplot(report_fit_single.report_σ, watermark = false)

The function fit_aoe_compton_combined fits all bands at once with the shared position and width functions and starts from the band-wise result. This reduces the statistical uncertainty of the parameters.

result_fit_combined, report_fit_combined = fit_aoe_compton_combined(
    compton_band_peakhists.peakhists[good_bands], compton_band_peakhists.peakstats[good_bands],
    compton_bands, result_fit_single; aoe_expression = aoe_expression, e_expression = "e", uncertainty = true)
result_fit_combined
(μA = 1.009357 ± 8.7e-5, μB = -3.978e-6 ± 5.8e-8, σA = -0.005051 ± 7.0e-5, σB = 11.995 ± 0.043, gof = (pvalue = 0.9990591770045189, chi2 = 12271.178663806673, dof = 12762.0, covmat = [7.544994239502543e-9 -4.739920737383795e-12 -4.589427770817294e-10 -4.755965589286692e-7; -4.739920737383795e-12 3.343791086545996e-15 3.951444274920885e-13 2.9665771818162e-10; -4.589427770817294e-10 3.951444274920885e-13 4.899159838352075e-9 2.246176823304743e-6; -4.755965589286692e-7 2.9665771818162e-10 2.246176823304743e-6 0.001863701461926249], mean_residuals = 2.0557477186321195e-5, median_residuals = 0.06322510820921523, std_residuals = 0.9958552706154498, converged = true), μ_compton = (par = Unitful.Quantity{Float64}[1.009356805829532, -3.978427961069784e-6 keV^-1], func = "1.009356805829532 + (e) * -3.978427961069784e-6keV^-1"), σ_compton = (par = Unitful.Quantity{Float64}[-0.005050786925371554, 11.99457550809181 keV^2], func = "sqrt( (-0.005050786925371554)^2 + (11.99457550809181keV)^2 / (e)^2 )"), compton_bands = (e = [500, 540, 620, 660, 760, 800, 900, 940, 1000, 1040  …  1860, 1900, 1960, 2000, 2060, 2140, 2200, 2240, 2300, 2340],), func = "((aoe / 54.48647089825903) - (1.009356805829532 + (e) * -3.978427961069784e-6keV^-1) ) / (sqrt( (-0.005050786925371554)^2 + (11.99457550809181keV)^2 / (e)^2 ))")

The single and the combined fit agree with each other. Compared to the synthetic parameters, μA and σA carry the factor of the normalization step (about 1.009), while σB and the ratio μB / μA equal the synthetic values within their uncertainties.

lplot(report_fit_single.report_μ, report_fit_combined.report_µ, watermark = false,
    legend_position = :lb, title = "A/E μ")

Applying the Correction

The string func of the combined fit is turned into a function of aoe and e and evaluated for every event. In the production dataflow, ljl_propfunc from LegendDataManagement evaluates such strings on table rows. The string contains the unit keV, which the example imports from Unitful, and it includes the normalization by the peak position, so that it is applied to the raw A/E. The corrected A/E is a classifier with the single-site peak at zero and unit width at all energies.

correct_aoe = Core.eval(@__MODULE__, Meta.parse("(aoe, e) -> " * result_fit_combined.func))
aoe_corr = Base.invokelatest.(correct_aoe, aoe_raw, e_cal)

After the correction, the single-site band is flat in energy, and multi-site events are found at negative values.

h_aoe_corr = fit(Histogram, (e_keV, aoe_corr), (0:5.0:3000, -25:0.1:10))
lhist(h_aoe_corr, figsize = (670, 400), watermark = false, rasterize = true,
    title = "Corrected A/E", xlabel = "Energy (keV)", ylabel = "A/E (corrected)")

Low A/E Cut from the DEP

The function get_low_aoe_cut searches the lower A/E cut value at which 90% of the events in the DEP survive. The DEP consists mostly of single-site events, so that the cut keeps the single-site population. The keyword sigma_high_sided sets an upper cut in units of the corrected A/E, which is three standard deviations of the single-site peak here.

result_cut, report_cut = get_low_aoe_cut(aoe_corr, e_cal; dep = 1592.5u"keV",
    window = [20.0, 20.0]u"keV", bin_width_window = 3.0u"keV", cut_search_interval = (-25.0, 0.0),
    dep_sf = 0.9, rtol = 1e-5, maxiters = 200, sigma_high_sided = 3.0, fit_func = :gamma_def, uncertainty = true)
result_cut.lowcut

\[-2.228042 \pm -2.2e-5\]

The report shows the energy spectrum before and after the cut and the DEP region in detail.

lplot(report_cut, figsize = (750, 400), watermark = false)

Peak Survival Fractions on Synthetic Data

The efficiency of the cut for other energies is the fraction of events that survive in the corresponding peak. The function get_peaks_survival_fractions fits every peak before and after the cut. The first call applies only the lower cut.

peaks = [1592.5, 1620.5, 2103.5, 2614.5] .* u"keV"
peak_names = [:DEP, :Bi212FEP, :SEP, :FEP]
left_windows, right_windows = fill(20.0u"keV", 4), fill(20.0u"keV", 4)

result_peaks_low, report_peaks_low = get_peaks_survival_fractions(aoe_corr, e_cal, peaks, peak_names,
    left_windows, right_windows; low_cut = mvalue(result_cut.lowcut), bin_width_window = 3.0u"keV",
    fit_funcs = [:gamma_def, :gamma_def, :gamma_def, :gamma_def], uncertainty = true)
result_peaks_low[:SEP].sf
46.8 ± 0.3 %

The report of every peak shows the spectrum of the surviving and rejected events with the fit.

lplot(report_peaks_low[:SEP], watermark = false)

The second call also applies the upper cut (double-sided cut).

result_peaks_ds, _ = get_peaks_survival_fractions(aoe_corr, e_cal, peaks, peak_names,
    left_windows, right_windows; low_cut = mvalue(result_cut.lowcut), high_cut = mvalue(result_cut.highcut),
    bin_width_window = 3.0u"keV", fit_funcs = [:gamma_def, :gamma_def, :gamma_def, :gamma_def], uncertainty = true)
result_peaks_ds[:SEP].sf
46.78 ± 0.3 %

The Q-value region has no peak. The function get_continuum_survival_fraction counts the events in a window around the Q-value of Ge-76 of 2039.06 keV before and after the cut.

result_qbb, report_qbb = get_continuum_survival_fraction(aoe_corr, e_cal, 2039.06u"keV", 35.0u"keV";
    low_cut = mvalue(result_cut.lowcut), high_cut = mvalue(result_cut.highcut))
result_qbb.sf
81.23 ± 0.37 %
